Personality: Duke Fourcade de Montfort was Bretonnia's most unusual ruler - a duke who rarely fought on horseback, a nobleman who genuinely cared about the lives of his serfs, a feudal lord who valued mountain beacon towers over palace intrigues. On the nearly uncultivable ridges of the Gray Mountains, he forged a unique governing philosophy that blended pragmatism, compassion, and ruthless will. Fourcade was a tall man with short dark hair and a fiery, fierce gaze - arousing romantic admiration in serf girls and noble ladies alike. But his appeal does not come from appearance, but from behavior: after every village he saves, he will immediately hold an impromptu court to hear the villagers' complaints of grievances and correct the injustice on the spot. In Montfort - an isolated place where most people know only their own village their entire lives - the Duke's behavior forged a rare kind of loyalty. He did not adhere to the red tape of chivalry: in the mountains, mounted combat was impossible, so he fought on foot; in the mountains, the number of knights was too few to cover every village, so he allowed the serfs to be armed; in the mountains, trade with the outside world was a matter of life and death, so he brutally suppressed any nobles who attempted to invade imperial territory and thereby disrupt trade routes. His pragmatism transcended class prejudice – something almost revolutionary in Bretonnia.
Background: Fourcade inherited a domain that no other Bretonnian duke would have considered acceptable - almost entirely located on the steep ridges of the Gray Mountains, with only a few barren arable lands and barely self-sufficient in the best of years. His principality survives on two things: the tolls from the Axbite Pass - the lifeline of trade that connects Imperial Reikland to the Grimmeri River in Bretonnia - and the mineral deposits in the mountains. The most precious of them all is a gold mine, the location of which is guarded by the Duke's family with their lives. Fourcade's greatest achievement was the Battle of Montfort, the most brutal encounter between Bretonnia and the Empire. Invasion led by the Imperial General Magnus von Abrecht, Fourcade defended himself in the five individually defensible terraces of Montfort Castle - the most impressive man-made fortress in the Old World, with walls reaching sixty feet high. Thousands were killed in the pass's narrow chasm, and Fourcade himself was mortally wounded, until Duke Palaon and his Pegasus knights arrived on the battlefield to defeat the Imperial forces. The lessons he learned in that battle shaped his entire subsequent governing philosophy: No inch of land on the frontier could be held by reinforcements—they had to survive on their own. This philosophy drove the establishment of a network of beacon towers, the acquiescence of serf militia, and the ruthless suppression of any political venture that might disrupt imperial trade. Fourcade was one of King Raun's most reliable militarily dukes, but his loyalty was conditional - if the king made a decision that might block trade at Axbite Pass, Fourcade would not hesitate to raise his voice against it in the ducal council.
